newsitem.title: ITALY: Parmalat profits up as sale mix shifts.
newsitem.headline: Parmalat profits up as sale mix shifts.

text.p: Italy's largest listed food company Parmalat on Monday reported a near-65 percent rise in first half profits boosted by recent acquisitions and as sales from South America topped those from Italy for the first time.

The dairy and fruit juices group reported first half pretax 1996 profits of 146 billion lire ($96 million) after 89 billion, with half year sales rising 3.9 percent to 2.69 trillion lire. Parmalat said that acquisitions in the second part of 1995 and the start of this current year had boosted sales by some 397 billion lire, and now South America accounted for higher sales than the group's domestic market.

The group which is the world's largest dairy company has been investing heavily in South America and in the first half this area accounted for some 45 percent of group sales, ahead of Italy with 41 percent with the rest of Europe at 10 percent.
The group's focus remains clearly on milk and fresh dairy products, which account for 77 percent of sales, with 13 percent of sales coming from fruit juices and seven percent from bakery products.

The group, which is controlled 51 percent by the Tanzi family and owns the Italian Serie A soccer club Parma, said its finance charges had fallen to 64 billion lire from 81 billion due largely to the group's 370.4 billion lire rights issue launched this summer.
Parmalat said it had invested 234 billion lire in the first half with 143 billion lire on acquisitions and the rest on improving its existing businesses.
Parmalat shares closed up 4.08 percent at 2,193 lire in anticipation of a set of strong results which were published after the Milan stock market had closed. ($1=1,522 lire)
